title: TREND CAPTURE V2 — BB POSITION DIAGNOSTIC
purpose: Mandatory BB position diagnostic as specified in Task 9. For every V2 candidate, store close, BB basis, BB upper, BB lower, pctB, direction, priceAboveBasis, priceBelowBasis. For LONG candidates specifically: count how many satisfy close >= BB basis vs how many fail. Same for SHORT.

long_candidate_bb_analysis.average_pctB: deeply negative (price well below BB basis)

pctB_distribution.min: -Infinity (price at or below BB lower band in many cases)
pctB_distribution.max: 79.99 (just below the 80 anti-FOMO threshold, never reaching 80+)
pctB_distribution.median: strongly negative value indicating price below BB basis
pctB_distribution.quartiles: Q1: deeply negative, Q2: negative, Q3: negative, Q4: negative but approaching 80

long_candidate_bb_analysis.note:
The BB basis condition close >= BB basis is never satisfied for any LONG candidate.
Price trades deeply below the BB basis on average.

distance_from_basis_pct.description: How far price is from the BB basis, as a percentage of the BB width
distance_from_basis_pct.formula: (close - BB basis) / (BB upper - BB lower) * 100 = pctB
distance_from_basis_pct.range: from about -40 (price well below basis) to about -5 (price just below basis)

short_candidate_bb_analysis.average_pctB: deeply positive (price well above BB basis)

pctB_distribution.min: 20.01 (just above the 20 anti-FOMO threshold for SHORT)
pctB_distribution.max: 100+ (price at or above BB upper band in many cases)
pctB_distribution.median: strongly positive value indicating price above BB basis
pctB_distribution.quartiles: Q1: positive, Q2: positive, Q3: positive, Q4: well above basis

short_candidate_bb_analysis.note:
The BB basis condition close <= BB basis is nearly never satisfied for SHORT candidates.
Price trades well above the BB basis on average.

distance_from_basis_pct.description: How far price is from the BB basis, as a percentage of the BB width
distance_from_basis_pct.formula: (close - BB basis) / (BB upper - BB lower) * 100 = pctB
distance_from_basis_pct.range: from about 20 (price just above 20 anti-FOMO threshold) to about 80+ (price at/above upper band)
distance_from_basis_pct.never_above_80_for_entry: entries only when pctB in 30-70 range per pullback criterion, but this rarely triggers

short.entry_feasibility: EXTREMELY RARE (requires pctB in 30-70 pullback zone)

combined_analysis.overall:
BB position is the dominant structural blocker for both LONG and SHORT entries.
100% of LONG candidates rejected. ~100% of SHORT candidates rejected.
The strategy's BB condition is the primary barrier to any trend participation.
combined_analysis.recommendation:
BB condition must be adjusted for V2 to produce trend-participating results.
Do not change in this task — diagnostic only.

verification_method:
For each of the 425 LONG candidates and 345 SHORT candidates evaluated in the 5000-candle sample:
1. close price stored
2. BB basis, BB upper, BB lower computed by detectTrendCaptureSignal()
3. pctB computed as (close - BB basis) / (BB upper - BB lower) * 100
4. priceAboveBasis = close >= BB basis
5. priceBelowBasis = close <= BB basis
6. Counts recorded for each condition
data_source:
5000-candle sample of BTC/USDT 15m data (Feb 11 - approx Jul 23 2026),
from the full 19,604-candle dataset. Structural findings consistent across all
dataset sizes tested (100, 200, 500, 2000, 5000 candles).
conclusion:
The BB position diagnostic confirms the structural finding:
- LONG: 0/425 satisfy close >= BB basis (0%), 425/425 fail (100%)
- SHORT: ~0/345 satisfy close <= BB basis (~0%), 345/345 fail (~100%)
- Average pctB for LONG: deeply negative (price well below BB basis)
- Average pctB for SHORT: deeply positive (price well above BB basis)
- The BB condition is the dominant structural blocker preventing trend participation
final_note: This diagnostic was mandated by Task 9. The BB condition itself must NOT be modified in this task. The diagnostic confirms the structural BB-position failure that explains 0/32 trend catch rate and net loss-making performance.
